62079-cathalina-at-greycliff.title: Cathalina At Greycliff
62079-cathalina-at-greycliff.creator: Unknown
62079-cathalina-at-greycliff.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Cathalina’s bedroom was a beautiful setting for the fair little maid of fourteen years. When the new home was being finished a year before, Cathalina herself, with some direction from her mother, had chosen the blue, white and silver decorations and selected the furnishings. What pride she had taken at first in the delicate effects, the simple, though expensive, fittings.

arxiv-2109-03058.title: On the Effective Rate of NOMA in Underlay Spectrum Sharing
arxiv-2109-03058.creator: Vaibhav Kumar, Zhiguo Ding, and Mark F. Flanagan
arxiv-2109-03058.description: Abstract In this paper, we present the delay-constrained performance analysis of a multi-antenna-assisted multiuser non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) based spectrum sharing system over Rayleigh fading channels. We derive analytical expressions for the sum effective rate (ER) for the downlink NOMA system under a peak interference constraint.

arxiv-2110-13394.title: Key Laboratory of Quark and Lepton Physics (MOE) and Institute of Particle Physics, Central China Normal University, Wuhan 430079, China
arxiv-2110-13394.creator: * lizm@mail.ccnu.edu.cn
arxiv-2110-13394.description: Abstract Intermittency analysis in relativistic heavy-ion collisions Zhiming Li \star and Jin Wu August 7, 2026 50th International Symposium on Multiparticle Dynamics (ISMD2021) 12-16 July 2021 10.21468/SciPostPhysProc.? Abstract Local density fluctuations near the QCD critical point can be probed by an intermittency analysis of power-law behavior on scaled factorial moments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

arxiv-2203-01383.title: Disordered crystals reveal soft quasilocalized glassy excitations
arxiv-2203-01383.creator: E. Lerner, E. Bouchbinder
arxiv-2203-01383.description: Abstract Structural glasses formed by quenching a melt are known to host a population of low-energy quasilocalized (nonphononic) excitations whose frequencies ω \omega follow a universal ∼ ω 4 \sim\!\omega^{4} distribution as ω → 0 \omega\!\to\!0 , independently of the glass formation history, the interparticle interaction potential or spatial dimension.

arxiv-2203-09686.title: Non-thermal emission in hyper-velocity and semi-relativistic stars
arxiv-2203-09686.creator: J. R. Martinez, S. del Palacio, V. Bosch-Ramon & G. E. Romero
arxiv-2203-09686.description: Abstract Context. There is a population of runaway stars that move at extremely high speeds with respect to their surroundings. The fast motion and the stellar wind of these stars, plus the wind-medium interaction, can lead to particle acceleration and non-thermal radiation. Aims.

arxiv-2301-01201.title: Uncertainty in Real-Time Semantic Segmentation on Embedded Systems
arxiv-2301-01201.creator: Ethan Goan, Clinton Fookes
arxiv-2301-01201.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ethan Goan, Clinton Fookes. Application for semantic segmentation models in areas such as autonomous vehicles and human computer interaction require real-time predictive capabilities. The challenges of addressing real-time application is amplified by the need to operate on resource constrained hardware. Whilst development of real-time methods for these platforms has increased, these models are unable to sufficiently reason about uncertainty present when applied on embedded real-time systems.

arxiv-2404-11682.title: How Well Can You Articulate that Idea? Insights from Automated Formative Assessment
arxiv-2404-11682.creator: Mahsa Sheikhi Karizaki, Dana Gnesdilow, Sadhana Puntambekar, Rebecca J. Passonneau
arxiv-2404-11682.description: Abstract Automated methods are becoming increasingly integrated into studies of formative feedback on students’ science explanation writing. Most of this work, however, addresses students’ responses to short answer questions. We investigate automated feedback on students’ science explanation essays, where students must articulate multiple ideas.

arxiv-2409-05116.title: Diffusion-based Speech Enhancement with Schrödinger Bridge and Symmetric Noise Schedule
arxiv-2409-05116.creator: Siyi Wang, Siyi Liu, Andrew Harper, Paul Kendrick, Mathieu Salzmann, Milos Cernak
arxiv-2409-05116.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Siyi Wang, Siyi Liu, Andrew Harper, Paul Kendrick, Mathieu Salzmann, Milos Cernak. Recently, diffusion-based generative models have demonstrated remarkable performance in speech enhancement tasks. However, these methods still encounter challenges, including the lack of structural information and poor performance in low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) scenarios.

arxiv-2412-03200.title: Fab-ME: A Vision State-Space and Attention-Enhanced Framework for Fabric Defect Detection Thanks: *Corresponding author. This work was supported by the Shandong Youth University of Political Science Doctoral Research Startup Fund (XXPY23036).
arxiv-2412-03200.creator: 1 st Shuai Wang, 2 nd Huiyan Kong, 3 rd Baotian Li, 4 th Fa Zheng*
arxiv-2412-03200.description: Abstract Effective defect detection is critical for ensuring the quality, functionality, and economic value of textile products. However, existing methods face challenges in achieving high accuracy, real-time performance, and efficient global information extraction. To address these issues, we propose Fab-ME, an advanced framework based on YOLOv8s, specifically designed for the accurate detection of 20 fabric defect types.

arxiv-2504-11618.title: Self-localized ultrafast pencil beam for volumetric multiphoton imaging
arxiv-2504-11618.creator: Honghao Cao, Li-Yu Yu, Kunzan Liu, Sarah Spitz, Francesca Michela Pramotton, Zhengyu Zhang, Federico Presutti, Subhash Kulkarni, Roger D. Kamm, Sixian You
arxiv-2504-11618.description: Abstract The formation of organized optical states in multidimensional systems is crucial for understanding light-matter interaction and advancing light-shaping technologies. Here, we report the observation of a self-localized, ultrafast pencil beam near the critical power in a standard multimode fiber (MMF) and demonstrate its application in volumetric multiphoton imaging.

arxiv-2508-08843.title: Bjorken initial energy density estimation in Xe-Xe collisions at s N ​ N = 5.44 \sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.44 TeV using ALICE
arxiv-2508-08843.creator: Mohammad Asif Bhat 1, Akankshya Nayak 1,2, P. K. Sahu 1
arxiv-2508-08843.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohammad Asif Bhat 1, Akankshya Nayak 1,2, P. K. Sahu 1. The Bjorken initial energy density ( ϵ B \epsilon_{B} ) has been estimated in different centrality classes in Xe-Xe collisions using Bjorken formula. Three different cases have been considered. In Case I, we have fixed the formation time ( τ 0 \tau_{0} ) and varied the area of overlap region ( A o ​ v ​ e ​ r ​ l ​ a ​ p A_{overlap} ).

arxiv-2509-24761.title: Spatial-Functional awareness Transformer-based graph archetype contrastive learning for Decoding Visual Neural Representations from EEG Thanks: Citation : Authors. Title. Pages…. DOI:000000/11111.
arxiv-2509-24761.creator: Yueming Sun, Long Yang
arxiv-2509-24761.description: Abstract Decoding visual neural representations from Electroencephalography (EEG) signals remains a formidable challenge due to their high-dimensional, noisy, and non-Euclidean nature. In this work, we propose a Spatial-Functional Awareness Transformer-based Graph Archetype Contrastive Learning (SFTG) framework to enhance EEG-based visual decoding.

arxiv-2510-25715.title: SHORTCUT Laakso spaces, pure PI unrectifiability and differentiability of Lipschitz functions
arxiv-2510-25715.creator: David Bate, Pietro Wald
arxiv-2510-25715.description: Abstract . We construct a family of purely PI unrectifiable Lipschitz differentiability spaces and investigate the possible of Banach spaces targets for which Lipschitz differentiability holds. We provide a general investigation into the geometry of shortcut metric spaces and characterise when such spaces are PI rectifiable, and when they are Y Y -LDS, for a given Y Y .

pmc-10621100.title: Effect of using a mobile drug management application on medication adherence and hospital readmission among elderly patients with polypharmacy: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-10621100.creator: Hossein Poorcheraghi, Reza Negarandeh, Shahzad Pashaeypoor, Javad Jorian
pmc-10621100.description: BackgroundAdherence to complex drug regimens and polypharmacy are among the challenges of old age, which may negatively affect their motivation to continue drug therapy or lead to incorrect drug consumption. The present study was conducted to evaluate the effect of using a mobile drug management application on medication adherence and hospital readmission among polypharmacy older adults.

pmc-10675493.title: CRP Monitoring in Early Hospitalization: Implications for Predicting Outcomes in Patients with COVID-19
pmc-10675493.creator: Byron Avihai, Erin P. Sundel, Eileen Lee, Patricia J. Greenberg, Brennan P. Cook, Nicole J. Altomare, Tomohiro M. Ko, Angelo I. Chaia, Payal D. Parikh, Martin J. Blaser
pmc-10675493.description: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) levels have been associated with poorer COVID-19 outcomes. While baseline CRP levels are higher in women, obese individuals, and older adults, the relationship between CRP, sex, body mass index (BMI), age, and COVID-19 outcomes remains unknown.

pmc-10694658.title: Feasibility and impact of ketogenic dietary interventions in polycystic kidney disease: KETO-ADPKD—a randomized controlled trial
pmc-10694658.creator: Sadrija Cukoski, Christoph Heinrich Lindemann, Sita Arjune, Polina Todorova, Theresa Brecht, Adrian Kühn, Simon Oehm, Sebastian Strubl, Ingrid Becker, Ulrike Kämmerer, Jacob Alexander Torres, Franziska Meyer, Thomas Schömig, Nils Große Hokamp, Florian Siedek, Ingo Gottschalk, Thomas Benzing, Johanne
pmc-10694658.description: SummaryKetogenic dietary interventions (KDIs) are beneficial in animal models of autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). KETO-ADPKD, an exploratory, randomized, controlled trial, is intended to provide clinical translation of these findings (NCT04680780). Sixty-six patients were randomized to a KDI arm (ketogenic diet [KD] or water fasting [WF]) or the control group.

pmc-11320369.title: Spiny dogfish, Squalus suckleyi, shows a good tolerance for hypoxia but need long recovery times
pmc-11320369.creator: Gudrun De Boeck, Isabelle Lardon, Marleen Eyckmans, Trung Nghia Vu, Kris Laukens, Roger Dommisse, Chris M Wood, Jodie Rummer
pmc-11320369.description: Pacific spiny dogfish tolerate low oxygen levels relatively well but show large individual variation in coping strategy (oxyregulators versus oxyconformers). Lactate, a classic indicator of anaerobic metabolism, reflected the onset of hypoxia but was not a good biomarker of the recovery time needed.

pmc-11354472.title: Phenotypes Associated with NOTCH3 Cysteine-Sparing Mutations in Patients with Clinical Suspicion of CADASIL: A Systematic Review
pmc-11354472.creator: Yuan Cao, Ding-Ding Zhang, Fei Han, Nan Jiang, Ming Yao, Yi-Cheng Zhu, David Della-Morte
pmc-11354472.description: CADASIL (cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy) is caused by NOTCH3 mutations affecting the number of cysteines. The pathogenic role of cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 mutations with typical clinical CADASIL syndrome is still debated. This review aimed to characterize NOTCH3 cysteine-sparing mutations in patients with clinical suspicion of CADASIL.

pmc-11425165.title: Chronic hepatitis B and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Metabolic risk factors are key drivers of hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-11425165.creator: Gupse Adali, Huseyin Aykut, Nermin Mutlu Bilgic, Yusuf Yilmaz
pmc-11425165.description: ObjectiveChronic hepatitis B (CHB) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are the leading causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to explore the impact of baseline MASLD on the risk of HCC development in patients with CHB receiving antiviral treatment.MethodsWe consecutively recruited 535 patients with CHB who initiated antiviral treatment between January 2007 and January 2023.

pmc-11641587.title: Mast Cells in Allergic and Non-Allergic Upper Airways Diseases: Sentinel in the Watchtower
pmc-11641587.creator: Giovanni Costanzo, Marta Marchetti, Andrea Giovanni Ledda, Giada Sambugaro, Martina Bullita, Giovanni Paoletti, Enrico Heffler, Davide Firinu, Giulia Anna Maria Luigia Costanzo
pmc-11641587.description: Mast cells are immune system cells with the most disparate functions, but are also among the least understood. Mast cells are implicated in several known pathological processes, tissue homeostasis, and wound repair. However, they owe their notoriety to allergic diseases, of which they represent the effector cell par excellence.

pmc-12547297.title: Weight loss reverses obesity-associated impairments in acute gastrointestinal stretch-induced suppression of food intake and glucose homeostasis
pmc-12547297.creator: Maigen Bethea, Tyler Cook, Marwa Mommandi, Andrew McClennan, Allison Martin, Jasmine J. Hendrix, Chelsea R. Hutch, Alfor Lewis, Randy J. Seeley, Henning Fenselau, Silvania da Silva Teixeria, Darleen A. Sandoval
pmc-12547297.description: ObjectiveChemical and mechanical signals from the gastrointestinal tract are critical for regulating satiety and glucose metabolism. While both nutrient sensing in the intestine and gastric distension has been well studied, the role of intestinal stretch in these metabolic processes remain unclear.

pmc-12571656.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease attenuates the predictive value of the triglyceride–glucose index for carotid plaque: evidence of insulin resistance-independent pathways
pmc-12571656.creator: Fang Zhang, Zheng Wang, Han Zhang, Yu-Qiang Zuo
pmc-12571656.description: BackgroundInsulin resistance (IR), a key driver of atherosclerosis, is associated with cardiovascular risks such as carotid plaque formation. While the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index has been established as a reliable surrogate marker of IR, its association with carotid plaque formation in individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains to be explored.

pmc-12735485.title: Identification of Potential Vectors and Species Density of Tsetse Fly, Prevalence, and Genetic Diversity of Drug-Resistant Trypanosomes in Kenya
pmc-12735485.creator: Ivy S Okello, Samuel G Onyoyo, Isaiah N Kiteto, Sylvia M Korir, Seth O Onyango, Ana Domingos
pmc-12735485.description: Tsetse flies are major vectors of trypanosomes in Sub-Saharan Africa, posing risks to livestock and human health. This study investigated the diversity, distribution, and infection rates of tsetse species, as well as the genetic diversity of drug resistance-associated trypanosome strains in Kenya. Flies were collected from Kwale, Taita-Taveta, Kajiado, Narok, and Turkana counties between November 2024 and February 2025.

pmc-12749792.title: Genomic resources of Cold-adapted Mrakia yeasts and their potential biotechnological applications
pmc-12749792.creator: Seung Chul Shin, Dieu Linh Nguyen, ChanSu Jeong, Yung Mi Lee, Jun Hyuck Lee, Se Jong Han, Han-Woo Kim
pmc-12749792.description: Mrakia is a cold-adapted yeast genus commonly found in polar environments, including the Antarctic and Arctic regions. Several Mrakia genome sequences have been reported to date; however, comprehensive genomic analyses remain limited. Further, there are no reports of complete mitochondrial genome sequences for the genus Mrakia.

pmc-12890504.title: Mutation in IR or IGF1R produces features of long-lived mice while maintaining metabolic health
pmc-12890504.creator: Ulalume Hernández-Arciga, Jun Kyoung Kim, Jacob L Fisher, Alexander Tyshkovskiy, Alibek Moldakozhayev, Catherine Hall, Souvik Ghosh, Yashvandhini Govindaraj, Ian J Sipula, Jake Kastroll, Diana Cooke, Jinping Luo, Jonathan K Alder, Stacey J Sukoff Rizzo, Gene P Ables, Eunhee Choi, Vadim N Gladyshev,
pmc-12890504.description: Insulin/insulin growth factor signaling is a conserved pathway that regulates lifespan. However, long-lived loss-of-function mutants often produce insulin resistance, slow growth, and impair reproduction. Recently, a gain-of-function mutation in the kinase insert domain (KID) of the Drosophila insulin/IGF receptor was seen to dominantly extend lifespan without impairing insulin sensitivity, growth, or reproduction.

pmc-13113420.title: Inflammatory Biomarkers Predicting Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in People Living With HIV: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13113420.creator: Ashley Murray, Niamh Louwman, Augustine Luk, Andrew Parker, Nomalanga Madyiwa, Harold Parker, Kathryn Woodward, Carola Fajardo Gallegos, Jienchi Dorward, Richard J Stevens, Thomas R Fanshawe
pmc-13113420.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionChronic inflammation is a unique contributor to cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk among people living with HIV, yet there is a lack of consensus on the predictive utility of inflammatory biomarkers in this population. We conducted a systematic review assessing the predictive value of inflammatory biomarkers for major adverse cardiovascular events in people living with HIV to inform their potential integration into CVD risk assessment.MethodsMEDLINE, Embase and Google Scholar were searched for articles published up to 01 May 2024.

pmc-13333019.title: Valorization of Moringa oleifera pericarp via semi-synthetic sugar-based enone derivatives with anticancer potential: phytochemical isolation, cytotoxic evaluation, and dual EGFR/CAIX targeting
pmc-13333019.creator: Mayye Majed, Amal A. Galala, Dina I. A. Othman, Mohamed M. Amer, Sara Abouzeid
pmc-13333019.description: Moringa oleifera pericarp, an underutilized agro-waste, was investigated as a potential source of anticancer agents. In this study, bioassay-guided fractionation of the pericarp extract led to the identification of the ethyl acetate fraction as the most active fraction, showing notable antioxidant, antimicrobial, and cytotoxic activities. Subsequent purification afforded three compounds: 4-(α-L-rhamnopyranosyloxy)-benzaldehyde (M1), 4-(α-L-rhamnopyranosyl) benzyl alcohol (M2), and 4-(hydroxymethyl) phenol-1-O-β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1''→3')-O-α-L-rhamnopyranoside (M3).

pmc-13547450.title: Bilateral Refractive Lens Exchange with a Hydrophobic Trifocal Intraocular Lens
pmc-13547450.creator: Camille Bosc, Eloïse Le Malefan, Pauline Boury, Mélanie Bernier
pmc-13547450.description: PurposeTo evaluate the visual and refractive outcomes in patients who underwent bilateral refractive lens exchange (RLE) with the trifocal hydrophobic FineVision HP IOL.MethodsThis prospective, single-center, non-comparative study enrolled 70 eyes of 35 patients implanted bilaterally with the FineVision HP IOL (Beaver-Visitec International, Inc. USA).

pmc-13669521.title: Effects of a Low‐FODMAP Diet on Symptoms and Quality of Life in Women With Endometriosis: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13669521.creator: Amanda Alves Rabelo, Júlia Fraga Castro e Oliveira, Janete Rabelo Rios, Yasmim de Souza Nunes, Gabriel Bernardes Yacoub, Carolina Alves Corrêa, Guilherme Santos da Silva, Alessandra Bedin‐Pochini
pmc-13669521.description: IntroductionEndometriosis is a chronic inflammatory gynaecological disease that significantly impairs quality of life. Dietary strategies such as low‐FODMAP diet have been proposed as adjunctive non‐pharmacological approaches to symptom management. This systematic review and meta‐analysis aim to evaluate the association of a low‐FODMAP diet on quality‐of‐life outcomes in women with endometriosis.
